J. M. Smucker beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $2.22 billion, up 5% year on year. It was an impressive quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and a solid beat of analysts’ EBITDA estimates.
Is J. M. Smucker a buy or sell going into earnings?

children: This quarter, the market is expecting J. M. Smucker’s revenue to decline 2.4% year on year, a reversal from the 2.6% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. J. M. Smucker has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at J. M. Smucker’s peers in the shelf-stable food segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. B&G Foods delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 4.7%, beating analysts’ expectations by 6.3%, and Hershey reported revenues up 3%, topping estimates by 0.8%. B&G Foods traded up 38% following the results while Hershey was also up 1.1%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the shelf-stable food segment, with share prices up 2.8% on average over the last month. J. M. Smucker is up 3.4% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $142.38 (compared to the current share price of $133.07).
